explanations.18: The replace() removes leading and trailing slashes from the URL path, and ?? '' provides an empty string as a fallback if the permalink doesn't exist.
explanations.23: This comment explains why voted starts as null instead of being read from localStorage immediately — it prevents React from seeing different HTML on the server vs. the browser.
explanations.32: The eslint-disable comment tells React's linter to ignore a rule that normally forbids reading localStorage in effects, because in this case it's intentional and safe.
explanations.34: The empty catch block silently ignores any errors (like localStorage not being available), allowing the component to work even when localStorage fails.
explanations.40: This line checks if the network response was successful (res.ok), and if so parses it as JSON, otherwise returns null to avoid crashing on bad responses.
explanations.63: The inner try-catch around localStorage.setItem gracefully handles the case where localStorage might not be available, without interrupting the vote submission.
explanations.70: The dependency array tells React to recreate handleVote whenever slug, apiUrl, or storageKey change, which prevents stale values from being captured inside the function.
explanations.89: The template literal concatenates two class names together — when voted, the button gets both the base btn style and the btnNeutral style for different appearance.
